candidate.title: Build decimal place value
prerequisiteAssumptions: Recognize tens and ones in whole numbers.

scenes.title: places: intro
scenes.learnerAction: Read the explanation and describe the place units in your own words.

content.body: We will explain how the value of a digit changes with its place, including places smaller than one.

accessibility.textAlternative: We will explain how the value of a digit changes with its place, including places smaller than one.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Read the paragraph in document order.

offline.note: Use the text and a notebook; capture written responses for later sync.

scenes.title: places: model
scenes.learnerAction: Read the explanation and describe the place units in your own words.

content.body: In 32.45, 3 represents thirty, 2 represents two, 4 represents four tenths and 5 represents five hundredths. Each place to the right has one tenth the value of the previous place.

accessibility.textAlternative: In 32.45, 3 represents thirty, 2 represents two, 4 represents four tenths and 5 represents five hundredths. Each place to the right has one tenth the value of the previous place.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Read the paragraph in document order.

offline.note: Use the text and a notebook; capture written responses for later sync.

scenes.title: places: guided
scenes.learnerAction: Explain the value of 3 in 24.36 using the place labels.

content.body: For 24.36, label tens, ones, tenths and hundredths. Then describe the value represented by 3.

scenes.learnerAction: Write 41.27 as a sum of place values and explain the value of 2.

content.body: Work alone. Write the number as a sum of its place values and explain what each digit represents.
